source.stem:
A concrete post is carried up a very high mountain. At the top of the mountain, the gravitational field is slightly weaker than at the bottom.
What is the effect of this weaker field on the mass and on the weight of the post at the top of the mountain?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The unit of weight is the kilogram.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A stretching one spring by 4 cm must weigh more than B stretching a different spring by 2 cm.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Stretching the spring further increases the Earth's pull on the same object.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The downward push of my hand on a book is the book's weight.

intelligence.enrichment: The weight of an object is the force with which the Earth pulls the object towards itself; weight measures how strongly the object is pulled by the Earth and is measured in newtons. Earth pulls object -> weight of object -> force value in newtons The learner correctly applies this rule: The weight of an object is the force with which the Earth pulls the object towards itself; weight measures how strongly the object is pulled by the Earth and is measured in newtons. Weight is the amount of matter in an object, so it should be written in kilograms even in science.
